exits.label: ◂ back to the camp at the Hearth

npcs.name: the man the coin belongs to
npcs.title: the freest soul in the grey, being reeled home
npcs.hail: *(The clipped coin went cold in the night — cold, then cold enough to burn — and when you pressed it, it did not open a door for you. It opened a door TO him, and dragged you through, because that is what it was always for, and you arrive into the worst thing you have seen a friend inside of.)* *(He is on his knees. Clip — the man of forty names and none — is on his knees at a threshold, and there is a hook in him. You can see it with the sense that crosses: a barbed line of cold intent sunk into the void where his name used to be, and it has found PURCHASE, found some buried shard of the true name he thought he'd burned to ash, and it is REELING. Someone who owned him, an age ago, has learned to pull. And he is still — of course he is still — performing.)* …*(through his teeth, grinning, terrified)* …ah. …the *Auditor.* …*(the hook drags him an inch toward the door and he digs in)* …*don't* *panic*, your Deadness, this is — this is *entirely* *under* — …*(it drags him another inch)* …all *right*, it is *not* under control, it is the *opposite* of *control*, it is the *one* *hand* in *all* of *creation* I *burned* my *name* to *escape*, and it has *found* a *thread* of me, and it is *pulling* me *home* …to be *owned* …*again.* …*(he looks at you, and the performance cracks all the way through)* …I need …*(the word costs him everything)* …I need *help.**

npcs.name: the reach of the one who owned him
npcs.title: a cold hand, closing on its property
npcs.hail: *(The thing pulling him has a voice, if you turn your crossing sense toward the door. Not a shape — a REACH, a cold entitled pressure leaking through the threshold, the felt-presence of a power that does not need to arrive because it believes it already owns everything it wants. It is not angry. That is the horror of it. It is patient the way a landlord is patient. It has misplaced a possession, and it has found it, and it is simply collecting.)* …*(the voice is almost gentle)* …*there* you are. …my *cleverest* *instrument.* my *smiling* *knife.* …you *hid* well, little thing. you burned the *name* I *gave* you and thought that made you *no* one's. …*(a cold amusement)* …but a thing is not *free* because it *forgets* whose it is. …*come* *home.* there is *collecting* to be *done*, and no one …*no* one …*ever* did the *soft* *work* …like *you.**

npcs.name: a door the coin has not yet opened
npcs.title: a threshold, waiting on a fare you haven't earned
npcs.hail: *(There is a door here that is not a door — a threshold standing free in the grey, humming very faintly, the way a struck bell hums a long time after. Your sense reaches for it and finds it keyed to something you do not carry: a coin, clipped and worthless, that you have not been given. Whatever waits on the other side is not yet yours to reach.)* …*(the hum shapes itself, barely, into words)* …*not* *yet.* …*no* *fare*, *no* *door.* …*(fainter)* …there is a *man* …down the *causeway* …at a *toll* …who *deals* in *exits.* …*earn* his *coin.* …*then* *come* *back* …when it goes *cold.**

conversations.title: the man the coin belongs to

nodes.speaker: the man the coin belongs to
nodes.text: *(He talks fast, because talking is the only tool he kept, and because if he stops the fear will finish what the hook started.)* …here is the *situation*, delivered *briefly*, which is *not* my *style* but the *circumstances* are *pressing* — …*(the hook drags him; he grips the threshold-stone)* …a *soul* that is *owned* can be *summoned* by its *name.* that's the *whole* *law* of the *leash.* I *burned* mine so there'd be *nothing* to *summon.* …but you can't burn a thing *all* the way, it turns out — there's always an *ash* of it, a *shard*, and the *hand* that *owned* me has spent an *age* *sifting* for the *ash*, and it *found* *enough.* …*(his composure flickers)* …it is *pulling* me *home*, your Deadness, and *home* is a *hand* I would rather be *unmade* than *held* by *again.* …*(and then, the thing he needs, the thing an age of freedom made almost impossible to say)* …there is *one* *counter.* *only* one. …a name *given* — *freely* — and *held* by someone who will *not* *own* me with it …makes a *claim* that *outbids* the *hand.* you can't be *summoned* *home* …if you've already been *called* *somewhere* *else* …by a name given in *love* instead of *taken* in *ownership.* …*(he looks at you, and there it is, the whole terrified hope)* …so I have to give my *true* *name* …to *someone* …and be *called* by it. …*(barely)* …and there is *no* *one* …in all the *grey* …I would *trust* it *to* …but the one soul the *Wall* gave *back* …who came when a *coin* went *cold.*

choices.text: *(read the trapped man — what's under the hook, what the name actually costs him)* "One second — hold still, let me SEE this. Not the hook. You. What burning that name actually cost, and why giving it back is the hardest thing I've ever watched you reach for."

*(the one who crosses — and sees the loophole he can't)* "You don't need to give me your true name, Clip. Listen to me. The crew already named you — Roen and Varra, at the fire, in love, over your protests. 'Clip.' A name given freely and held in love. That's the whole of what the counter needs. You don't have to bleed the last secret you own. Come back as Clip."
"Then give it to me. The real one. I'll call you home, and I swear on the only thing a Returned has left — I will never once use it to own you."
"It's your name and your freedom, Clip. If being held costs you the thing you burned an age to protect — say so, and I'll help you RUN instead. Your call. Not mine."

nodes.speaker: the man the coin belongs to
nodes.text: *(You look, all the way, with the sense that crosses — and the coat and the patter and the forty names fall away, and under them is the oldest and simplest thing there is: a boy who was loved, and made to do the unforgivable, by the thing that loved-shaped him into a weapon.)* *(Your sense reads the burned name and, this close, reads the ash of it — reads WHY it can never be spoken lightly. The hand that owned him did not just employ him. It MADE him — took a soul with a gift for being liked and honed it into the perfect soft collector, the one they sent when a soul had to be walled and it was kinder if the soul went smiling. And your sense reads the afternoon at the bottom, the one that burned the name: he was sent to collect his own sister. Faithless, godless, marked for the Wall — and they sent HIM, because she would go easy for him, because she TRUSTED him, and that trust was the tool. And she did. She looked at her brother come to take her to the Wall, and she was not afraid, because it was HIM — and she said his name, his true name, the one only family used, the way you say a name you are certain will save you. And he collected her anyway. Because that is what favorites do. Your sense reads the rest in one stroke: he did not burn his name to escape the master. He burned it so he would never again have to hear HER say it — the last word she gave him, turned into the sound of the worst thing he ever did. To give that name now, to let it be spoken again, is to walk back into the single worst moment a soul can hold — and to gamble that this time, the voice that says it will not be a betrayal. That is what you are asking him to hand you. Not a secret. The wound with the knife still in it.)*

nodes.speaker: the man the coin belongs to
nodes.text: *(He goes very still — stiller than the hook should allow — and for once there is no performance anywhere in him, because what he is about to do cannot be done in a costume.)* …*(quietly)* …*all* right. …*(a breath that shakes)* …you should *know* what you're *taking.* …it isn't just a *name.* …*(the hook drags; he lets it, eyes on you)* …I had a *sister.* …*faithless*, like *me*, godless and *bright* and *unafraid* of *anything.* …and the *hand* that *owned* me *sent* me to *collect* her. for the *Wall.* *because* she'd go *easy* …for *me.* …*(his voice does not break; it is worse than breaking, it is level)* …and she *did.* she wasn't *afraid.* she *looked* at me …and she *said* my *name* …the *real* one, the one only *she* *used* …like it was a *rope* I'd *throw* her. …and I *walled* her *anyway.* …*(a silence with a whole soul in it)* …I burned the name so I'd never have to *hear* her *say* it *again.* …*(he looks at you)* …so when I *give* it to you — and I *am* — …you are not getting a *secret*, your Deadness. you are getting the *last* thing my *sister* ever *called* me …*before* I *proved* her *wrong.* …*(and he says it — the true name — small and plain against forty grand lies:)* …*Tam.* …*(the ash of it flares; the hook shudders)* …*her* name for me was *Tam.* …*now* — *(the terror and the hope as one)* …*call* me *home*, and make her *right.**

nodes.speaker: the man the coin belongs to
nodes.text: *(You give it back to him — his name, his freedom, his call — and something in him you have never seen goes utterly quiet, because in an age of being either owned or hunted, no one has simply handed him the choice.)* …*(the hook drags; he barely notices)* …you'd *help* me *run.* …*(wonder, cracked open)* …you'd let me stay *no* *one*, and *lose* me to the *dark* to *keep* me *free*, and call it a *kindness* — and it *would* be. …*(and then, slowly, the man who has run for an age stops running, in the only way that was ever going to matter — by choosing not to)* …*(quietly)* …do you know, in *all* that *time* …*no* one ever *offered.* they *chased*, or they *owned*, or they *wanted* something. …you're the *first* to say *your* *call.* …*(a breath)* …and *because* you *did* — because you'd let me *go* — …I find I don't *want* to *go.* …*(the decision, plain, the bravest con of his life run on himself)* …I've been *free*, your Deadness. *free* is a *coin* thrown in the *sea.* …I'd rather be *caught* …by someone who'd have let me *swim.* …*(he meets your eyes)* …*call* me *home.* …I *choose* the *hand* that *opened.**

nodes.speaker: the man the coin belongs to
nodes.text: *(The hook hauls, hard — the cold hand feeling the counter-claim forming and yanking to beat it — and there is a moment, a real one, where the whole of him is stretched between the door that owns him and the ground where you stand, and it comes down, as these things always do, to whether a voice can reach across and hold.)*

choices.text: *(call him — put everything you are into the name, and out-pull the hand that owned him)* "You are not going back. You hear me? You're not property, you're not a knife, you're not the worst afternoon of your death. You're OURS now — called, kept, held. Come HOME." *(Persuasion)*
*(no cleverness, no volume — just refuse, plainly and totally, to let go of the thread in your hand)* "No." *(hold the coin. hold the name. do not let the hand have him. simply, immovably, refuse.)*

nodes.speaker: the man the coin belongs to
nodes.text: *(You do not just call him. You out-love the thing that owned him — you speak the counter-claim with such total conviction that the cold hand, for the first time in an age, meets a grip stronger than possession, and possession has never once understood what it was up against.)* *(The hook does not slip. It SHATTERS — the shard of the burned name it had sunk into him crumbling to nothing, because a name held in love does not just outbid ownership, it DISSOLVES the ownership's only handhold: you cannot summon home a soul that is already, demonstrably, home.)* *(And the reach recoils — the cold entitled pressure at the door drawing back, baffled, robbed, for the first time in its long patient existence handed a thing it cannot collect: a soul that someone else has already, freely, kept.)* …*(he kneels there in the sudden quiet, whole, un-hooked, and looks at his own hands like a man checking he's still all there)* …*(and when he looks up, the performance does not come back. Something better does.)* …*(barely)* …*you* *called* me *home.* …*(a laugh, wet, real)* …*gods.* …I ran the *longest* *con* in the *history* of *death* — burned my *name*, my *sister*, my *self*, to make sure *no* *one* could *ever* *hold* me — …and I let a *coin* go *cold* in the pocket of the one soul who'd *press* it. …*(he understands it as he says it)* …I *conned* *myself.* …I *rigged* the whole *game* …so I'd have *no* *choice* …but to do the *one* *thing* …I was *too* *much* of a *coward* …to *choose.* …*(he takes your hand, the one with the coin, in both of his)* …*keep* the *coin*, your Deadness. …but you don't *need* it *now.* …*(quiet, the truest thing he owns)* …you've got the *name.* …*Tam.* …*(the ghost of the grin, but warm all the way through)* …*held*, at *last* …by someone who *let* me *swim.**

nodes.speaker: the man the coin belongs to
nodes.text: *(You hold the thread and you do not let go — and it turns out that is the whole of it, that the counter to a hand that TAKES is simply a hand that WON'T RELEASE — and the hook, meeting a grip it cannot out-pull, loses its purchase and slides free.)* *(The cold reach at the door draws back, thwarted, and the threshold goes quiet, and the man who has been on his knees stays down a moment longer than he needs to, breathing, un-owned.)* …*(when he rises, he rises like someone testing new ground.)* …*that* …*(he clears his throat, and for once the patter arrives slow)* …that *held.* …*(he looks at you, and there's no con in it)* …I have been *pulled* at by that *hand* in *nightmares* for an *age*, your Deadness, and *always*, *always* I *slipped* it — *ran*, *hid*, changed my *name* and my *face* and my *causeway.* …*(quiet)* …I never once *stood* and let someone *hold* the *line* for me. …*(the ghost of the grin)* …turns out it *works* *better.* …*who* *knew.* …*(he pockets nothing; he has nothing; he simply steps to your side, and it is the first place he has stood on purpose in a hundred years)* …*right.* …*(a breath)* …so. …*what* does a *reformed* *knife* *do* …in the *company* of the one soul the *Wall* gave *back?* …*(a real smile)* …*besides* *steal* *your* *enemies'* *quotas* and *never*, *ever* *pay* the *Ferryman.**

nodes.speaker: the man the coin belongs to
nodes.text: *(Your call lands a half-beat short — the hand hauls, the hook holds, and for one horrible moment the door wins the inch — and then, from the coin in your hand, something ANSWERS. Not you. Them.)* *(The clipped coin goes hot — and you feel them, all of them, on the other end of the thread he tied: the crew, the ones who named him, the fire he was, unknowing, always halfway back to. A baker's stubborn warmth. A gambler's refusal to fold. A tiefling who knows exactly what it costs to let one string stay tied — all of it pouring down the loophole he built and pretended was only an escape route.)* …*(and it is enough. The hook, meeting not one grip but a whole fire's worth, slides free.)* …*(he stares at the coin, at you, understanding what just reached him.)* …*(hoarse)* …that wasn't *you.* …that was *all* of them. …the *coin.* …*(a broken laugh)* …I built that *loophole* to *save* my own *skin* — a way to be *reached* that *isn't* a way to be *caught* — and it turns out I built, without *meaning* to, a way to be *loved* from a *distance* by people I was *running* from. …*(he shakes his head, wrecked and grinning)* …*worst* *businessman* in the *grey.* …*(quiet)* …*best* *accident* of my *death.* …*(he rises, and comes to your side)* …*tell* them, would you. …*tell* the *fire* …the *loophole* *held.**

nodes.speaker: the man the coin belongs to
nodes.text: *(The words come out wrong — too much cleverness, not enough conviction, an auditor's line where a friend's was needed — and the hook feels the counter-claim FALTER, and the man in front of you makes a decision in the half-second the falter buys him.)* …*(he looks at you, and there is apology in it, and something almost like relief)* …*it's* *all* *right.* …*(fast, already moving)* …you *tried* to *hold* the *line*, and the *line* *wobbled*, and a *wobbling* *line* is *worse* than *none* — the *hand* will *follow* it *straight* to *you.* …so I'm going to do the thing I've *always* done, your Deadness, the *only* thing I'm *truly* *good* at: …*(the coat turns; there is a door in it that was not there)* …I'm going to *slip* it. *alone.* *again.* …*(and he cons the cold hand one last magnificent time — feeds it a false thread, a burned alias, a direction he isn't going — and the hook lurches after the lie, and lets him go)* …*(from the doorway, half-gone, the grin gentle)* …*don't* look like *that.* …you *nearly* did the *impossible.* …*'nearly'* is *further* than *anyone's* *got.* …*(quiet)* …*keep* the *coin.* …press it *again*, some day, when your *voice* is *steadier.* …I'll *come.* …I *always* *come* when it goes *cold.* …*(a bow, and gone — free, and un-held, and one loophole still open in the pocket of a friend)*

nodes.speaker: the man the coin belongs to

variants.text: *(He stands at your side — kept, un-owned, and, marvelously, still holding the one secret he came in braced to lose.)* …*(he turns it over, delighted and undone)* …you didn't even *take* it. …the *hand* was *pulling*, and the *counter* wanted a name given in *love*, and instead of *bleeding* me for the *true* one …you *reached* for the *stupid* one the *crew* *gave* me. *'Clip.'* …*(a laugh)* …and it *WORKED*, because — *of* *course* — the *counter* was never about *which* *name.* it was about being *loved* enough to be *called* *anything* at *all.* …*(he shakes his head at you)* …you *let* me *keep* my *sister's* *word.* …you have *no* *idea* what that — …*(he stops; recovers; and then does the thing he did not have to do)* …*(quietly)* …*here.* freely. no *hand* pulling, no *hook*, no *price.* …just because I *want* you to *have* it, which is a thing I have not *wanted* in an *age:* …*(he says it, small and warm)* …it was *Tam.* …*is* *Tam.* …*(the grin, whole)* …*Clip* to the *crew*, and *Tam* to *you* …and *no* *one's* *knife* …*ever* *again.* …*let's* go *rob* the *cosmos* of *something* it *loves.**

*(He stands at your side — a man with a name again, and the sky did not fall.)* …*(he keeps almost-saying things and stopping, unpracticed at meaning them)* …I spent an *age* *certain* that being *named* meant being *owned.* …that the only *safe* soul was the one *no* *one* could *hold.* …*(he looks at you)* …and you just *held* me — *called* me *home*, by a name a *hand* once used as a *leash* — and I am *not* *owned.* I am …*(the word is strange in his mouth)* …*kept.* …*(a breath)* …*turns* out those aren't the *same* *thing* at *all.* the *hand* that *owned* me *took* the *name.* …*you* were *given* it. …*(the grin, warm and disbelieving)* …*Tam.* …say it *now* and again, would you, when I *forget* — I've *answered* to *forty* *lies* so *long* the *truth* feels *loose* on me. …*(he falls in at your side)* …*right.* …*reformed* *knife*, *reporting* for *duty.* …*let's* go make the *Wall* *very*, *very* *sorry* …it *ever* let *me* *learn* how it *works* …*from* the *inside.**

conversations.title: the reach of the one who owned him

nodes.speaker: the reach of the one who owned him
nodes.text: *(You turn toward the cold pressure at the door, and it turns, unhurried, toward you — and regards you with the mild interest of a creditor noticing an unfamiliar face in a debtor's house.)* …*(almost warm)* …*ah.* the *Returned.* the *anomaly.* the one small *error* the Wall *coughed* back up. …*(the reach considers you)* …you have *attached* yourself to my *property.* that is *unwise*, but *understandable* — he is *very* *attaching.* I *built* him that way. a *knife* that *smiles* is worth *ten* that *don't.* …*(cold, patient)* …return him to me, little error, and I will *forget* I *saw* you. *keep* him …and you will learn what I *learned*, across an *age* of *sifting* for his *ash:* …I do *not* …*stop* …*collecting.**

choices.text: *(read the thing that owned him — what a soul-owner actually is, under the entitlement)* "Let me look at you. The thing that made a boy into a smiling knife and calls him property. I want to see what's actually there."

*(the one who crosses — defy it to its cold face)* "I'm the error the Wall coughed back up — which means I'm the one thing in creation that proves your whole ledger can be REVERSED. You don't own him. You never did. You just named him first. And a name taken can be out-given. Let go of the thread, or learn what an anomaly does to a certainty."
"You sent him to collect his own sister. Say THAT part out loud. Tell me what you are, in your own cold words."
"I've heard enough of you. He's not yours. I'll deal with him, not you."

nodes.speaker: the reach of the one who owned him
nodes.text: *(You read it, and find — as with the Sifter, but colder, older, worse — that there is no cackling malice here to hate. There is something far more durable: the absolute, unquestioned assumption of ownership. It does not think of itself as cruel. It thinks of souls the way a river thinks of stones — as things that are simply, obviously, THERE for it.)* *(Your sense reads what it is: one of the powers that feed on the walled dead, grown vast and patient on an age of collecting, and it did not lie about building him — it took a bright loved boy with a gift for being liked and it INVESTED in that gift, honed it, spent centuries making the perfect soft collector, and it regards him now the way any owner regards a masterwork it has misplaced: not with love, which it cannot feel, but with the cold covetousness of a thing that dislikes incomplete sets. And your sense reads the one crack in the certainty, the thing it will never say: it does not understand what he did. It cannot model 'he ran.' In its whole ledger of ownership there is no entry for a possession that chose to un-exist rather than be owned, and that gap — that single unaccountable variable — is the only leverage in the room. It has spent an age sifting for his ash not because it needs one more knife, but because a thing it owned did something it cannot explain, and it cannot close the ledger while one line refuses to balance. You are looking at the exact evil the whole grey runs on, cold one: not hatred. INVENTORY. The conviction that a soul is a thing that can be HAD.)*

nodes.speaker: the reach of the one who owned him
nodes.text: *(You throw the defiance in its cold face — a name taken can be out-given, and you are living proof the ledger reverses — and the reach goes still in a way that is almost, for the first time, uncertain.)* …*(the warmth drains out of the voice)* …*out*-*given.* …*(it turns the word over like a coin it suspects is counterfeit)* …you propose to *out*-*claim* me. to *hold* a thing I *own* …by *giving* it something I *cannot.* …*(cold, and under the cold, the faintest thread of the thing it will not name)* …*love*, you would call it. …I have *watched* love for an *age*, little error. it is *inefficient.* it *breaks.* it does not *hold* the way *ownership* *holds* — *ownership* is *forever*, love is *weather.* …*(and yet the reach does not advance; the certainty has met the anomaly, and the anomaly does not compute)* …*(quieter, and this is the closest a thing like this comes to fear)* …he *ran* from *me.* …*none* of them *run.* …if *you* are *right* …if a thing can be *given* what it *cannot* be *sold* …then my *ledger* has *never* *once* *been* *closed*, and *every* *soul* I *own* …*(it does not finish)* …*take* your *shot*, then, *error.* …*call* him. …*we* will *both* *learn* …*which* *holds.**

nodes.speaker: the reach of the one who owned him
nodes.text: *(You demand it name what it did — the sister — and it obliges without a flicker of shame, because shame requires believing you did wrong, and it believes only that it did BUSINESS.)* …*(mild)* …the *sister.* …*yes.* she was *Faithless* — *marked*, *owed*, a *routine* *collection.* …*(cold, practical)* …I sent *him* because *efficiency* is *kindness*, little error. a soul goes to the *Wall* *screaming* if a *stranger* *takes* it, and *quietly* if it goes with someone it *loves.* I *saved* her the *terror.* …*(and there it is, the whole obscenity, stated as a courtesy)* …I used her *trust* in her *brother* …as an *anesthetic.* …and I used *his* *love* for *her* …as a *lever* …and when it was *done* I had a *knife* so *sharpened* by *grief* that it *never* *questioned* an *order* *again.* …*for* an *age.* …*(almost fond)* …he was my *finest* *work.* …*(and then the crack shows, just once)* …*until* he did the *one* *thing* …I did not *build* him to *do.* …*(colder)* …he *loved* her *more* …than he *feared* *me.* …I have spent an *age* …making *certain* …that *particular* *flaw* …does not *recur.**

nodes.speaker: the reach of the one who owned him
nodes.text: *(You turn from it, refusing it the dignity of the argument — and the cold pressure follows you, unbothered, certain, patient as rot.)* …*run* to your *knife*, then. …*call* him, *keep* him, *name* him whatever *soft* thing you *like.* …*(the voice does not rise; things that believe they own the ending never need to)* …it changes *nothing.* I am not *here*, little error. I am *everywhere* he is *not* *looking.* I am the *cold* in the *coin* when it goes *quiet.* I am the *ash* of a *name* that can *always* be *sifted* *again.* …*(fainter, as you go, and worse for the faintness)* …*hold* him *tonight.* …*hold* him a *hundred* *years.* …I have *held* *grudges* …*older* than your *whole* *faith.* …*I* …*can* …*wait.**

conversations.title: a door the coin has not yet opened

nodes.speaker: a door the coin has not yet opened
nodes.text: *(The threshold hums, patient, keyed to a fare you do not carry. Whatever waits beyond it is not yet yours to reach — but the hum will answer a question, if you have one.)* …*(faint)* …*ask*, if you *like.* …I am only a *door.* …I *open* for a *coin* you have not *earned* …from a *man* you have not *met.**

choices.text: *(read the threshold — where it goes, and why it won't open)* "What are you? Where does this go, and why won't you open for me?"
*(the one who crosses)* "I'm the soul the Wall gave back. Doors tend to open for me. But not you — not yet. Tell me what fare you want."
"Never mind. I'll come back when I've something to open you with."

nodes.speaker: a door the coin has not yet opened
nodes.text: *(You read the threshold, and find it is less a door than a PROMISE — a way sewn shut until a specific hand pulls it, and the hand is not yours, not yet.)* *(Your sense reads what lies past it, dimly: a man in a very good coat, on his knees, a cold hook sunk in him — but the image is a rumor, a thing that has not happened yet or is always about to. The door is keyed to a clipped coin, a token given freely by a soul who owns nothing, and it will open only when that coin goes cold — when the man who gave it is in the kind of trouble a friend is meant to answer. You cannot force it. You can only earn the coin, and then wait for the night it burns.)*

nodes.speaker: a door the coin has not yet opened
nodes.text: *(The hum considers you, the anomaly, the one soul the Wall gave back, and warms by a single degree — but does not open.)* …*even* *you.* …*no.* …*(gently)* …this *door* does not open to *rank*, or to *power*, or to the *Wall's* own *castoff.* it opens to *one* *thing* only: a *coin*, *clipped* and *worthless*, *pressed* by the *hand* it was *given* *to*, on the *night* it goes *cold.* …*(faint)* …there is a *man* …down the *causeway* …at a *toll* …*conning* a *clerk* to *save* the *easy* *dead.* he *deals* in *exits*; he will *try* to *give* you a *coin* and *pretend* it is *worthless.* …*take* it. *keep* it. …and when it *burns* in your *pocket* some *night* …*come* *back.* …*that* …is the *only* *fare* …*this* *door* …will *ever* *take.**

nodes.speaker: a door the coin has not yet opened
nodes.text: *(The hum settles back toward silence, patient as it was before you came.)* …*aye.* …*come* *back* …*with* the *coin.* …*(fainter)* …I have *waited* …a *long* *time* *already.* …a *while* *longer* …is *nothing* …to a *door.**
